data.content_ref: inline:SRC_003 proposes a 'shares mechanism' relation between SRC_001's checklist effect and SRC_005's blind spot, naming cognitive narrowing/atomization as the shared mechanism. But the problem asks for a substantive relation whose REFUTED IF condition must genuinely threaten the claimed relation. The stated refutation—'an increase in checklist granularity is shown to restore edge-case sensitivity rather than further masking it'—only refutes a monotonic-narrowing sub-claim, not the 'shared mechanism' relation itself. Two artifacts can share a mechanism (cognitive narrowing suppresses holistic pattern perception) even if, in some regime, increasing granularity reverses the narrowing; the shared mechanism at the endpoint level is consistent with a non-monotonic granularity curve. Thus the refutation condition is mis-specified: it attacks a stronger claim (monotonicity) that is not the relation being proposed, so the 'refuted if' does not actually test the shared-mechanism relation.
